description: hamopy is a Python package for the numerical simulation of one-dimensional coupled heat, air and moisture (HAM) transfer in porous materials, solving the conservation equations by the finite-element method. It was written by Simon Rouchier of Université Savoie Mont-Blanc; release v0.2.0 was archived on Zenodo on 9 June 2015. Its original field is the hygrothermal modelling of building materials. Users can add materials and customise their property equations, account for liquid and vapour water flow and storage, apply time-dependent boundary conditions, run fully coupled hygrothermal or thermal-only simulations, and automate many runs for sensitivity analysis or evolutionary algorithms; the only dependency is SciPy. Coverage: any wall or material layer that can be treated in one dimension. Access: source on GitHub, documentation on GitHub Pages and the v0.2.0 archive on Zenodo. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): LGPL-3.0. Free. Caveats: one-dimensional only, and the archived release dates from 2015. Simulation uses: moisture and condensation risk in envelope retrofits and flood-wetted walls, and calibration against hygrothermal measurements. Related records: the timber-framed wall hygrothermal measurements and the double-skin façade validation data.
